context.analysis:
## Overview
[System screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time and provides case management for analysts. Built for a mid-size payment processor in AWS eu-west-1.]

## Key Elements
- Merchant / Payment Gateway (API Client)
- Fraud Analyst and Risk Operations Manager
- Compliance Auditor / Regulators
- Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening System (AWS Boundary)
- External Identity Provider (IdP)
- AWS S3 / Glacier (Cold Storage)

## Relationships
- Merchant to System: gRPC/REST over TLS for sub-50ms authorization scoring
- Analysts to System: HTTPS via Web UI for case management
- System to IdP: OAuth2/OIDC for multi-factor authentication
- System to S3/Glacier: AWS SDK/IAM for 7-year tamper-evident audit logs

## Technology Stack
- AWS API Gateway & Route 53: Ingress routing and health checks for <50ms P99 latency and fail-open availability
- AWS CloudWatch & CloudTrail: Native observability and PCI-DSS Level 1 compliant log monitoring
- AWS S3 / Glacier: Immutable storage for 7-year audit retention within budget
- AWS CodePipeline: Blue/green deployments for zero-downtime model updates

## Rationale
[Native AWS managed services minimize operational overhead for a three-engineer team while ensuring PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance. Using serverless and cloud-native primitives guarantees performance targets within the strict 25,000 EUR monthly budget.]

containers.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud at scale and provides a case management interface for analysts. It operates within strict compliance, latency, and budget constraints on AWS.

## Key Elements
*   **Users:** Fraud Analyst, Risk Operations Manager, Compliance Auditor
*   **External Systems:** Merchant / Payment Gateway, External Identity Provider (IdP)
*   **Containers:** API Gateway (AWS API Gateway / ALB), Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go-based ECS Fargate), Case Management Backend & UI (React + Node.js/Python on ECS Fargate)
*   **Data & Storage:** Feature Store (Amazon ElastiCache Redis), Audit Log Storage (Amazon S3 with Object Lock and Amazon Athena)

## Relationships
*   Merchant / Payment Gateway to API Gateway via REST/HTTPS
*   API Gateway to Real-Time Scoring Engine via REST/HTTPS
*   Real-Time Scoring Engine to Amazon ElastiCache Redis via Redis Protocol
*   Real-Time Scoring Engine to Amazon S3 via S3 API (HTTPS)
*   Fraud Analysts to Case Management UI via REST/HTTPS

## Technology Stack
*   **Compute:** AWS ECS Fargate for lightweight, containerized microservices and UI hosting.
*   **Scoring & Rules:** Go for the Real-Time Scoring Engine with embedded in-memory rule evaluator and static ONNX model binaries.
*   **Caching:** Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) for sub-millisecond feature lookups.
*   **Audit & Compliance:** Amazon S3 with Object Lock paired with Amazon Athena for tamper-evident 7-year audit logs.
*   **Infrastructure & DevOps:** Terraform for Infrastructure as Code and automated CI/CD pipelines.

## Rationale
This architecture uses serverless and managed AWS services to minimize operational overhead, enabling a three-engineer team to maintain the system within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget. Go containers, embedded rules, and Redis ensure the strict P99 latency below 50 ms at 3,000 TPS.

API Gateway.analysis:
## Overview
The system screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real-time and provides a case management interface for analysts. It ensures PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance while maintaining sub-50ms latency at 3,000 transactions per second within a fixed AWS budget.

## Key Elements
- Merchant / Payment Gateway
- External Identity Provider (IdP)
- API Gateway (AWS API Gateway / ALB, AWS WAF)
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go, AWS ECS Fargate, ONNX)
- Case Management Backend & UI (React, Node.js / Python, ECS Fargate)
- Feature Store (Amazon ElastiCache Redis)
- Audit Log Storage (Amazon S3, Amazon Athena)

## Relationships
- Merchant / Payment Gateway -> API Gateway: Sends payment authorizations [HTTPS / TLS 1.3]
- API Gateway -> Real-Time Scoring Engine: Forwards payment authorizations [gRPC over TLS]
- Case Management UI -> Case Management Backend: Manages review cases [HTTPS]
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Feature Store: Retrieves real-time fraud features [Redis Protocol]
- Audit Log Storage -> AWS S3 / Athena: Stores tamper-evident audit records [AWS SDK / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- AWS API Gateway & ALB: Managed edge routing, rate limiting, and TLS termination
- AWS ECS Fargate: Serverless container orchestration for low-overhead service management
- Go: High-performance backend execution for ultra-low latency real-time scoring
- Amazon ElastiCache Redis: In-memory data store for real-time feature retrieval
- Amazon S3 & Athena: Secure, durable audit log storage and query capabilities

## Rationale
The architecture combines managed AWS edge services with containerized Go microservices to meet strict sub-50ms latency and PCI-DSS compliance requirements. This lean design minimizes operational toil, enabling a three-engineer team to operate the platform reliably within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget.

Real-Time Scoring Engine.analysis:
## Overview
The Real-Time Payment Fraud Screening system evaluates card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud under 50 ms to prevent checkout fraud while ensuring high availability. It processes high-throughput transactions on AWS while maintaining PCI-DSS Level 1 compliance and 7-year auditability.

## Key Elements
* HTTP/gRPC Ingress Router (Go container component)
* Feature Assembler (Go container component)
* Inference & Rule Executor (Go + ONNX Runtime C-API)
* Audit Dispatcher (Go container component)
* Model & Rule Synchronizer (Go background goroutine component)
* Amazon ElastiCache Redis (Feature Store)
* Amazon S3 (Audit Log and Model Storage)

## Relationships
* API Gateway -> HTTP/gRPC Ingress Router: Forwards payment authorizations [REST/HTTPS]
* Feature Assembler -> Amazon ElastiCache Redis: Retrieves transaction features [Redis Protocol]
* Inference & Rule Executor -> Model & Rule Synchronizer: Atomically swaps model references via `atomic.Value` [In-memory]
* Audit Dispatcher -> Amazon S3: Flushes asynchronous audit payloads [S3 API / HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
* Go: Chosen for ultra-low latency and minimal memory footprint to meet the <50 ms P99 requirement.
* ONNX Runtime C-API: Enables high-performance execution of compiled machine learning models.
* Amazon ElastiCache Redis: Provides low-latency, in-memory feature retrieval at 3,000 TPS.
* Amazon S3: Delivers cost-effective, tamper-evident storage for audit logs and model binaries.

## Rationale
This architecture achieves sub-50 ms P99 latency at 3,000 TPS within a 25,000 EUR monthly budget by utilizing single-service containerization with in-memory Go concurrency. Strict decoupling of asynchronous auditing, read-only Redis patterns, and atomic model hot-swapping ensure high availability and zero-downtime updates.

Case Management Backend & UI.analysis:
## Overview
The Case Management system provides an interactive React UI and Python backend enabling fraud analysts to review suspicious payment cases and manage workflows. It ensures compliance-driven auditability while maintaining real-time queue synchronization.

## Key Elements
* **React Analyst Web App**: Single-page application hosted on Amazon S3 and distributed via Amazon CloudFront.
* **FastAPI Case Management Backend**: Unified container handling API routing, RBAC, data masking, and orchestration on AWS ECS Fargate.
* **Audit Event Emitter**: Internal module using AWS SDK (boto3) to stream immutable logs.
* **Audit Log Storage**: Amazon S3 featuring Object Lock for tamper-evident retention.

## Relationships
* **Fraud Analyst -> React Analyst Web App**: Reviews flagged transactions and manages queues via HTTPS and WebSockets.
* **React Analyst Web App -> FastAPI Case Management Backend**: Communicates request data and queue updates via REST/HTTPS and WebSockets.
* **FastAPI Case Management Backend -> Amazon S3**: Streams append-only audit events via AWS SDK over HTTPS.

## Technology Stack
* **Python (FastAPI)**: Consolidated backend runtime reducing maintenance overhead for a 3-person team.
* **React**: Frontend framework delivering sub-minute case reviews.
* **AWS ECS Fargate**: Serverless container orchestration fitting the 25k EUR monthly budget.
* **Amazon S3 with Object Lock**: Cost-effective, immutable storage satisfying the 7-year audit mandate.

## Rationale
This architecture minimizes operational complexity for a three-engineer team by consolidating runtime stacks. It meets strict PCI-DSS and 7-year audit requirements within budget through native AWS services.

Feature Store.analysis:
## Overview
[System screens card-not-present payment authorizations for fraud in real time and provides a case management system for analyst reviews. Core purpose is ensuring sub-50ms fraud detection while maintaining PCI-DSS compliance and 7-year auditability.]

## Key Elements
- **Users**: Fraud Analyst, Risk Operations Manager, Compliance Auditor
- **External Systems**: Merchant / Payment Gateway, External IdP, Amazon S3 / Glacier
- **Containers**: AWS API Gateway / ALB, Real-Time Scoring Engine, Case Management Backend & UI, Amazon ElastiCache Redis (Feature Store), Amazon S3 / Athena (Audit Log Storage)
- **Feature Store Components**: Feature Retrieval API, Feature Snapshotter, Feature Ingestion Worker, Feature Definition Registry

## Relationships
- **Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Feature Retrieval API**: Fetches online features [Redis Protocol]
- **Feature Snapshotter -> Audit Log Storage**: Flushes immutable feature vectors [HTTPS / S3 API]
- **Case Management Backend -> Audit Log Storage**: Queries historical snapshots [Amazon Athena]
- **Merchant -> API Gateway**: Submits payment authorization requests [HTTPS]

## Technology Stack
- **Compute**: AWS ECS Fargate (scalable container orchestration for a 3-person team)
- **Languages**: Go (high-performance scoring engine and retrieval API), Python (feature ingestion, snapshotting, and machine learning models)
- **Databases & Caching**: Amazon ElastiCache Redis (sub-millisecond feature lookups with Multi-AZ and `volatile-lru`), PostgreSQL / AWS RDS (feature definition registry and case management)
- **Audit & Storage**: Amazon S3 and Amazon Athena (tamper-evident 7-year audit logging and querying)
- **Security**: AWS KMS and TLS (encryption at-rest and in-transit for PCI-DSS compliance)
- **Infrastructure as Code**: Terraform (fully automated provisioning within the 25,000 EUR monthly budget)

## Rationale
[This architecture uses managed AWS services and ECS Fargate to minimize operational overhead for a three-person team while strictly enforcing PCI-DSS compliance. ElastiCache Redis and Go containers guarantee sub-50ms P99 latencies, while asynchronous S3 snapshots ensure immutable 7-year auditability within the 25,000 EUR budget.]

Audit Log Storage.analysis:
## Overview
The system provides real-time fraud screening for card-not-present payment authorizations, combined with tamper-evident audit logging for compliance. It ensures secure processing and case management while maintaining a fixed infrastructure budget and strict regulatory adherence.

## Key Elements
- Real-Time Scoring Engine (Go, AWS ECS Fargate, ONNX)
- Audit Buffer Component (Amazon SQS)
- Audit Ingestion Component (AWS Lambda)
- Tamper-Evident Vault Component (Amazon S3 with Object Lock and Lifecycle Rules)
- Query & Access Component (Amazon Athena)
- Compliance Auditor / External Regulators

## Relationships
- Real-Time Scoring Engine -> Audit Buffer: Enqueue payloads via SQS API (HTTPS)
- Audit Buffer -> Audit Ingestion Component: Consume log events via AWS internal polling
- Audit Ingestion Component -> Tamper-Evident Vault Component: Persist partitioned immutable logs via S3 API
- Compliance Auditor -> Query & Access Component: Run compliance queries via AWS Console / JDBC via Athena

## Technology Stack
- Amazon SQS: Decouples the scoring engine from storage spikes to protect P99 latency
- AWS Lambda: Serverless ingestion ensuring cost efficiency for a 3-engineer team
- Amazon S3 Object Lock: Enforces WORM compliance mode for 7-year tamper-evident audit retention
- Amazon Athena: Serverless SQL querying over partitioned data for rapid auditor reporting
- Amazon S3 Lifecycle Rules: Transitions data to Glacier Flexible Archive to maintain budget limits

## Rationale
This serverless-first audit architecture guarantees 7-year tamper-evident PCI-DSS compliance without human intervention or excessive operational overhead. Decoupling storage via SQS and S3 lifecycle tiering strictly protects the 50ms latency SLA while remaining well under the €25,000 monthly budget limit.
